description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Basic Electrical Engineering topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: basic-electrical

facts.claim: KCL: current into a node equals current out (algebraic sum zero)

source.quote: the sum of currents flowing into that node is equal to the sum of currents flowing out of that node

facts.claim: KVL: the sum of voltages around a closed loop is zero

source.quote: The directed sum of the potential differences (voltages) around any closed loop is zero

facts.claim: Any linear network → one voltage source in series with one resistance

source.quote: the theorem allows any one-port network to be reduced to a single voltage source and a single impedance

facts.claim: R_th: replace voltage sources by short circuits and current sources by open circuits

source.quote: if all ideal voltage sources in the circuit were replaced by a short circuit and all ideal current sources were replaced by an open circuit

facts.claim: In a linear circuit the total response is the sum of responses to each source alone

source.quote: the net response caused by two or more stimuli is the sum of the responses that would have been caused by each stimulus individually

facts.claim: Applies only to linear systems

source.quote: for all linear systems

facts.claim: Time constant τ = RC

source.quote: τ = RC is the time constant

facts.claim: After one τ the capacitor is about 63.2% charged; about 5τ to fully charge

source.quote: So the capacitor will be charged to about 63.2% after τ, and is often considered fully charged (>99.3%) after about 5τ

facts.claim: For a sine wave V_peak = √2 × V_rms (V_rms ≈ 0.707 V_peak)

source.quote: which implies VP = VRMS × √2, assuming the source is a pure sine wave

facts.claim: Example: 120 V mains has a peak of about 170 V

source.quote: Thus the peak value of the mains voltage in the USA is about 120 × √2, or about 170 volts

facts.claim: Power factor = real power / apparent power

source.quote: The power factor is defined as the ratio of real power to apparent power

facts.claim: Apparent power = V_rms × I_rms

source.quote: Apparent power is the product of root mean square (RMS) current and voltage

facts.claim: Star and delta networks are equivalent when terminal impedances match

source.quote: For equivalence, the impedance between any pair of terminals must be the same for both networks

facts.claim: Named after the shapes Y and Δ

source.quote: The name derives from the shapes of the circuit diagrams, which look respectively like the letter Y and the Greek capital letter Δ

facts.claim: Phases are 120° apart

source.quote: each of the three phases is offset by 120 degrees of phase shift relative to the others

facts.claim: Line-to-line (line) and line-to-neutral (phase) voltages

source.quote: The voltage between any two line conductors is called line-to-line voltage

facts.claim: A changing primary current makes a changing flux that induces an emf in the secondary

source.quote: A varying current in the transformer's primary winding creates a varying magnetic flux in the transformer core

facts.claim: Voltage ratio equals turns ratio

source.quote: The transformer winding voltage ratio is equal to the winding turns ratio

facts.claim: The rotor always turns slightly slower than synchronous speed

source.quote: an induction motor always operates slightly slower than synchronous speed

facts.claim: Slip: difference between synchronous and rotor speed (a few per cent)

source.quote: The difference, or "slip," between actual and synchronous speed varies from about 0.5% to 5.0%

facts.claim: A commutator and brushes connect the rotating armature coils to the supply

source.quote: The commutator allows each armature coil to be energized in turn and connects the rotating coils with the external power supply through brushes

facts.claim: The spinning armature produces a back (counter) emf

source.quote: the armature must turn faster to produce sufficient counter-EMF to balance the supply voltage

facts.claim: An RCD/ELCB trips when it detects leakage current

source.quote: RCDs are designed to disconnect the circuit if there is a leakage current

facts.claim: Typically trips at about 30 mA within milliseconds to prevent electrocution

source.quote: to detect small leakage currents (typically 5–30 mA) and disconnecting quickly enough (<30 milliseconds)

facts.claim: A buck converter steps DC voltage down

source.quote: A buck converter or step-down converter is a DC-to-DC converter which decreases voltage

facts.claim: Output voltage = duty cycle × input voltage

source.quote: the output voltage of the converter varies linearly with the duty cycle for a given input voltage
